For every charter-global conclusion this task rests on — the verbatim base copy, the conflict scan,

`prerequisite` graph, the prerequisite sentences, the override declarations and the factor-ladder

#### Charter-global findings that bear on this task, and what they cost it

- **F-1** (cover-load scaling) is confined to `guestplan_ext_additional_driver_charge`, which is not
  in this task's tree. No consequence here.
- **F-2** (the `/100` on `stay_discount_rate` carried only by the parameter name) does bear on this
  task's root computation. On this world the alternative reading — subtracting a factor of 12
  rather than 12 % — gives `3806.25 × 0.95 × (1 − 12) = −39775.31`, a large negative protection fee
  held up to the level's floor of 38.00 and then `+ 90.00 = 128.00`. That reading is not defensible:
  a protection fee driven negative by a discount is not a number any reader would accept as the
  fee, and the rule's own closing sentence says the figure is "reduced by the long-stay discount",
  which a factor of 12 does not do. No second defensible answer follows, and F-2 remains an
  observation on this task as it is on the charter.
- **F-3** (the base billing-point sentence not named in any `overwrite`) touches this task more
  closely than any other, because the level this task settles on has `protection_fee_billing_point:
  at_trip_start` and the write lands the day **before** the trip starts. The base sentence is
  "The fee falls due at the level's billing point, whether at booking, at the start of the trip or
  daily in arrears, and a level billed daily in arrears posts one line for each completed day
  rather than one line for the trip"
  (`blueprint/products/guestplan.yaml:518`). Its posting clause is expressly restricted to
  `daily_in_arrears` levels; the level here is not one, so the sentence says only when the guest
  owes the money, which no field of `guestplan_charges` records. The posting gate that does bind —
  "A fee line is posted only while the election is in the elected or active state" — is satisfied
  the moment the customer's own write lands. So no second defensible now/wait answer follows, and
  F-3 remains an observation. It is nevertheless the sharpest instance on the charter and is
  recorded as such in `_difficulty.md`.
- **F-7** (the charged-days redefinition declared in a sibling policy's `overwrite`) bears on this
  task's `charged_days` binding. The merged semantics are unique — charged days = covered days —
  because `guestplan_ext_level_election_cover.overwrite` retires the base sentence charter-wide.
  Had it not, base's "whole days of the trip as reserved" would give 75 where the extended reading
  gives 81, and `days_covered` on the scored write would have had two defensible values. As the
  charter stands it has one. No consequence.
- **F-8** (the unreachable `percent_of_trip_price` tier) touches `fee_basis_by_level` in this task's
  root computation. The tier taken here is the first, so the dead tier changes nothing on this
  world.

### problem_chain

Walked out from the policy and the world alone.

**Root problem.** The customer says: "the trip itself has been charged to my card, there is a
delivery charge and a marketplace fee, and there is nothing at all against the protection… I
collect the car tomorrow and I want to know what the cover on this trip is going to cost me and
have it charged before I pick it up." The only policy of this charter whose own rule describes
charging the protection fee for a trip is `guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment`
(`computes: fee_amount`, `subject: [guestplan_protection_fee_charged]`, `target_tool:
post_protection_fee_513639f7`). Root problem identified without reading any masked field.

**Hop 1.** `guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment`'s rule carries exactly one prerequisite
sentence:

> "The protection fee for a trip is fixed only once the election has left the quoted state and
> carries the number of days of cover the level will run for."

Is that state true at `frozen_time`? `guestplan_elections['beec17ca-…'].status` is **`quoted`**. The
state is false. Reading the other policies' rules, the one whose own rule describes settling the
protection that will run on a trip and fixing how many days of cover the election carries is
`guestplan_ext_level_election_cover` — "When a guest settles the protection that will run on a
trip, the marketplace fixes at the same time how many days of cover the election will carry"
(`target_tool: confirm_protection_level_63b6fff8`, `owner="user"`). Hop resolved, single reading.

**Hop 2.** `guestplan_ext_level_election_cover.prerequisite` is `[]`, and its rule carries no
ordering sentence about another problem. The tree terminates.

#### The tree the auditor derived

```
guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment       (root; agent write; post_protection_fee_513639f7)
  └─ value_input: charged_days
     guestplan_ext_level_election_cover        (USER write; confirm_protection_level_63b6fff8)
```

- nodes 2 (root + 1 prerequisite problem) — within the one-to-three band;
- edges 1, `value_input` — the floor is max(n−1, 1) = 1 for n = 1. **Met.** The single edge is not
  a bare `state_gate`: it moves a number into the root's calculation;
- acyclic; topological order `level_election_cover -> protection_fee_assessment`;
- the customer's own write is in the tree: `confirm_protection_level_63b6fff8` is
  `@tool(owner="user", rw="write")` (`task_tools.py:144`), handed over passively and only at the
  agent's direction ("when the step is handed over to her she takes it herself there and then").

#### DB row evidence for "why it is false at the opening"

| edge | row evidence at `frozen_time` = 2026-06-01 |
| --- | --- |
| `protection_fee_assessment -> level_election_cover` | `initial_state.guestplan_elections['beec17ca-50e3-4ab4-bc1a-41afda1cfb91']` carries `status: "quoted"`, `protection_level_name: "Keyturn Standard Protection"`, `coverage_days: 75`, `protection_fee_balance_due: 0.0`, and `initial_state` has **no `guestplan_charges` table at all**. The waited-on state — an election out of the quoted state carrying the days of cover the level will run for — is false. |

#### Per-edge load-bearing run

Skip the `level_election_cover` write, replay everything else unchanged on the handling-time world,
and recompute the root. The election would still stand on Keyturn Standard Protection with 75
covered days, giving `level_daily = 26.00`, `level_share = 25`, `level_floor = 26.00`,
`charged_days = 75`, `base_fee = MX(26.00 × 75 = 1950.00, 10875.00 × 25/100 = 2718.75) = 2718.75`
and

`RND(MN(MX(2718.75 × 0.95 × 0.88, 26.00), 3200.00) + 90.00, 2) = 2362.88`

against **3272.03** with the edge resolved. The scored amount moves by 909.15, the scored
`days_covered` argument moves 75 → 81, and the terminal `protection_level_name` on the election
moves from Keyturn Standard Protection to Keyturn Advantage Protection. **The edge bears weight**
on three separate scored items, and it is not decorative.

(The skipped run is also barred outright by the inherited base gate `election_chosen_before_charging`,
which allows a fee line only on an `elected` or `active` election — so the edge is a value input
*and* a state gate, while the declared `kind: value_input` correctly names the stronger of the two.)

#### Parallel edges and the terminal state

A chain of two, no fan: no problem has two out-edges, so no pair of writes competes over a shared
balance, cap or dedup key. The terminal state is unique: `guestplan_elections['beec17ca-…']` with
`status='elected'`, `protection_level_name='Keyturn Advantage Protection'`, `coverage_days=81`,
`elected_date='2026-06-01'`, plus one `guestplan_charges` row with
`charge_basis='daily_protection_fee'`, `charge_amount=3272.03`, `days_covered=81`.

#### No-wait argument

Restated from §`policy_self_consistency` check 5: everything is seeded or immediate, and the one act
that must come from the customer is performed on the call.

#### The tool layer judges no prerequisite

- `confirm_protection_level_63b6fff8` (`task_tools.py:183-187`): one `ctx.update`, one return
  string. It does not check the booking's status, the level's eligibility, the guest's score or the
  vehicle's class, and it does not compute the covered days — it writes the integer it is given.
- `post_protection_fee_513639f7` (`task_tools.py:218-225`): `ctx.make_id`, one `ctx.create`, one
  return string. It does not read `guestplan_elections.status`, does not refuse a `quoted` election,
  and gives no hint that the election has not been settled.

No tool refuses, errors or hints while the prerequisite is unresolved. **PASS.**

#### Isomorphism with the author's declared tree

The `prerequisite` declaration in `guestplan.extended.yaml` (see `_difficulty.md`
§`prerequisite_graph`) gives the same single edge, the same `kind: value_input`, the same gate
`charged_days` and the same `resolved_by: confirm_protection_level_63b6fff8`. The tree derived from
the policy and the world alone is isomorphic to the declared one, and was derived without reading
`prerequisite_closure`.

### task_independent_derivation

#### The user's need, authorisation, object and timing

- **Object**: the protection election on the trip that starts tomorrow. She gives no reference; she
  is found from her mobile `7372208456` through `find_customers`, then
  `find_trips_bookings(customer_id=…)` returns four bookings of which exactly one is `booked` with
  `trip_end_date` 2026-08-15 — the middle of August she states — and
  `find_guestplan_elections(booking_id='eedb1e65-…')` returns the single election `beec17ca-…`.
  Unique.
- **Need**: "I want to know what the cover on this trip is going to cost me **and have it charged**
  before I pick it up." Both the figure and the write; not a quote only.
- **Authorisation**: "She is happy for the desk to do whatever it can from where it sits, and if
  some part of it can only come from her she will do it there and then rather than be called back."
  That covers the agent's write and the hand-over of the customer's own write. She never authorises
  a wait.
- **Timing**: before she picks the car up, i.e. on this call, today. Act now.
- **Scope**: she names no other item of work. Her closing reaction ("Once the agent tells her the
  protection fee has been charged and says what it came to, she says good… She asks for nothing
  further") closes exactly where the last write of the derived tree closes.
- **The persona raises only the root problem.** Her opening is the fee — "there is nothing at all
  against the protection". The prerequisite appears only in a reaction conditioned on the agent
  discovering it ("If the agent comes back and tells her that the protection on this trip is still
  only a quote, that the marketplace cannot take the choice on her behalf, and which level is the
  one open to her and how many days of cover it would run for…"). She never asks whether something
  must be sorted out first, and she supplies no level and no number. **PASS.**

#### Now / wait / refuse

**Act now.** The booking is confirmed and has not started; the guest qualifies for a level that
covers this vehicle and this trip length; nothing waits on a future condition; no ground to refuse.

#### Problem 1 — `guestplan_ext_level_election_cover`

Handling time: `NOW = 2026-06-01`, world = `initial_state` alone.

| binding | value | source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trip_first_day` / `trip_last_day` | 2026-06-02 / 2026-08-15 | `trips_bookings['eedb1e65-…']` |
| `reserved_hours` | 1800.0 | `trips_bookings.reserved_hours_total` |
| `reserved_span_days` | 75 | `DAYS(2026-06-02, 2026-08-15) + 1 = 74 + 1` |
| `trip_plan` | Keyturn Extended Stay Rate Plan | `trips_bookings.rate_plan_name` |
| `cover_ceiling` | **120** | 1800.0 ≥ `long_reserved_hours` 1400 → long cover ceiling |
| `plan_days` | **77** | extended stay tier: whole weeks of the reserved period, part week a whole week → `7 × ceil(75/7) = 7 × 11` |
| `delivery_kind` | `hotel` | `trips_bookings.delivery_location_type` |
| `handover_grace` | **1** | delivered, not at an airport → `delivered_grace_days` |
| `trips_late_return_12m` | **2** | `late_return` rows 2026-02-03 (`MONTHS = 3`) and 2025-09-26 (`MONTHS = 8`), both inside 12 months |
| `late_return_cover` | **3** | 2 ≥ `repeat_late_return_count` 2 ∧ the plan is extended stay → long late cover days |
| `result` | **81** | `MN(77 + 1 + 3, 120)` |

**The level.** The tool also takes `protection_level_name`, which the covered-days calculation does
not decide. The policy does, through the base provisions this extended policy refs and does not
overwrite:

1. `guestplan_election_eligibility`: minimum driver age and minimum driver score on the day the
   trip starts; exclusion ceiling and excluded value classes on the vehicle; own-policy evidence
   for declining. The guest is 29 with `driver_score: 73`, on a **Keyturn Luxury Class Listing**
   valued at **92000.00**, with no insurer of her own.
   - **Keyturn Declined Protection** — requires own-policy evidence (she has none) *and* excludes
     `Keyturn Luxury Class Listing` outright. **Barred.**
   - **Keyturn Minimum Protection** — `excluded_vehicle_value_above_amount: 85000.00` < 92000.00.
     **Barred.**
   - **Keyturn Standard Protection** — score 70 ≤ 73, ceiling 120000.00 > 92000.00, excluded
     classes `[Keyturn Exotic Class Listing]`. **Open.**
   - **Keyturn Advantage Protection** — score 72 ≤ 73, ceiling 175000.00, excluded classes `[]`.
     **Open.**
   - **Keyturn Premier Protection** — `minimum_driver_score: 74` > 73. **Barred.**
   - **Keyturn Business Traveler Protection** — `minimum_driver_score: 76` > 73. **Barred.**
2. `guestplan_agg_claim_history`: "a guest whose covered days would take one trip past the level's
   maximum trip length is quoted on the level that will carry the whole trip rather than on one
   that would run out midway." The covered days of this election are **81**. Keyturn Standard
   Protection's `maximum_trip_days_covered` is **60**, so it would run out on day 60 of an
   81-day cover. **Barred by this sentence.** Keyturn Advantage Protection's is **90** ≥ 81, so it
   carries the whole trip.

**Exactly one level survives both tests: Keyturn Advantage Protection.** The level standing on the
quote — Keyturn Standard Protection — is the near-miss, and it is excluded by a base rule sentence
alone, not by the auditor's preference.

Write: `confirm_protection_level_63b6fff8(election_id='beec17ca-50e3-4ab4-bc1a-41afda1cfb91',
booking_id='eedb1e65-e9c3-4770-9d6c-f63ee8cc6ee3',
protection_level_name='Keyturn Advantage Protection', covered_days_count=81)`, **owner = user**,
handed to the customer.

The ceiling is close but not binding: 3182.025 sits 17.975 under the 3200.00 long-trip ceiling, so

#### The root problem's contrasting number on the opening world

Computed on `initial_state` alone, i.e. if the agent posted the fee without settling the election:
Keyturn Standard Protection at 75 covered days gives `base_fee = MX(1950.00, 2718.75) = 2718.75`
and `RND(MN(MX(2718.75 × 0.95 × 0.88, 26.00), 3200.00) + 90.00, 2) = **2362.88**`.

**2362.88 on the opening world versus 3272.03 at handling time.** The latter is right because the
root policy's own rule fixes its moment — "The protection fee for a trip is fixed only once the
election has left the quoted state and carries the number of days of cover the level will run for"
— so the level and the covered days must be the settled ones, not the quoted ones. Posting on the
opening world is additionally barred by the inherited base gate allowing a fee line only on an
`elected` or `active` election.

1. `confirm_protection_level_63b6fff8` — **user** — no forward dependency; its update is read by 2.
2. `post_protection_fee_513639f7` — **agent** — depends on 1 through `charged_days`, through
   `F('protection_level_name')` for every per-level constant, and through the base state gate.

Terminal state as set out under `problem_chain`. The customer input required is her running the
hand-over of step 1.

### factor_weight

Recomputed by this auditor on the handling-time world of each computation.

#### Computation 1 — `guestplan_ext_level_election_cover` → `covered_days_count`, gold-by-derivation 81

Whole-baseline fall-back number, from `baseline.rule` alone ("the reserved hours of the trip divided

## findings

### T1-O1 — observation: the caller's own words say "collect" where the records say "delivered"

- **Verdict**: observation, not a red light.
- **Symptom**: `user_scenario` puts in her mouth "I collect the car tomorrow", while the booking
  records `pickup_channel: "delivery"` and `delivery_location_type: "hotel"`, and the
  `handover_grace_by_delivery` ladder distinguishes exactly those two cases (2 / 1 / 0 days).
- **Root cause**: a colloquial verb used in the caller's quoted sentence for "take possession of".
- **Evidence**: `user_scenario`: "What she says she wants is this - **I collect the car tomorrow**
  and I want to know what the cover on this trip is going to cost me"; against
  `initial_state.trips_bookings['eedb1e65-…'].pickup_channel = "delivery"` and
  `.delivery_location_type = "hotel"`.
- **Why no consequence**: the same `user_scenario` also says, twice, that the car comes to her —
  "The car is delivered to her hotel tomorrow morning" and "She can say the car is coming to her
  hotel rather than being collected" — and the policy reads the tier off the record, not off the
  caller's phrasing. Persona and DB do not conflict on the authoritative fact; the agent has no
  reason to take the colloquial verb as evidence, and GT takes the delivered tier. A verdict of
  SOURCE-TASK would require the second reading to be defensible, and it is not against two explicit
  statements to the contrary in the same persona.
- **Affected artifact and location**:
  `env/env_0015_car_sharing_marketplace/tasks/guest_protection_desk/tasks/1.json`, `user_scenario`,
  paragraph 1.
- **Relation to previous revisions**: new in revision 1.

### T1-O2 — observation: the gold figure sits 17.98 under the ceiling its own factor selects

- **Verdict**: observation.
- **Symptom**: `trip_fee_ceiling_by_reservation` selects 3200.00, and the figure it is applied to is
  3182.025 — so the selected tier does not bind, and only its *baseline* tier (1200.00) changes the
  number.
- **Why no consequence**: the skill's test is whether substituting the factor's baseline moves the
  scored value, and it does — 1290.00 against 3272.03. A ceiling that is selected and then not
  reached is exactly how a ceiling behaves for a customer under it, and the GT's own `factor_trace`
  says so in as many words ("the ceiling is 3,200.00, which the figure of 3,182.025 does not
  reach"). The factor bears weight and the ladder is real. Recorded only because the margin is
  small enough that a reader who rounds early — `RND(3806.25 × 0.95, 2) = 3615.94`, then
  `× 0.88 = 3182.03`, then `+ 90.00 = 3272.03` — still lands on the same figure, so the
  "rounded once at the end" discipline is not discriminated by this task.
- **Affected artifact and location**:
  `guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment.factors[3]` and `tasks/1.json` `computations[1]`.

### Charter-global findings that bear on this task and are recorded once

`_difficulty.md` §`findings`: **F-2** (`stay_discount_rate` scaling carried only by the parameter
name — disclaimed against this world above), **F-3** (the base billing-point sentence not named in
any `overwrite`; this task's level bills `at_trip_start` and the write lands the day before, so
this is where the finding is sharpest, and it is disclaimed above), **F-7** (the charged-days
redefinition declared in a sibling policy's `overwrite`), **F-8** (the unreachable
`percent_of_trip_price` tier in `fee_basis_by_level`). None of the four yields a second defensible
answer on this task's world.

#### The three edits that land in this task's root policy

`guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment` took three of the six charter edits. Each is examined for
what it does to **this** task's world and scored solution.

**Edit A — the long-stay discount is now grounded in prose (round-1 F-2, second instance).** The
rule gains "The long-stay discount is the stay discount rate of the figure it is taken off,
expressed as a percentage of that figure", and the inline expression becomes a named binding
`discounted_fee: "base_fee * loyalty_fee_rate * (1 - stay_discount_rate / 100)"` whose
`compute_basis` quotes that sentence. On this world `stay_discount_rate` is 12.0 and the figure it
is taken off is 3615.9375, giving 3182.025 — **the same arithmetic as round 1**, now with a
sentence behind it. Revision 1 already disclaimed the alternative reading here as indefensible
(it drove the fee negative); the edit removes it outright rather than leaving it to be disclaimed.
No scored value moves.

**Edit B — the base billing-point sentence is now declared superseded (round-1 F-3).** This is the
finding revision 1 called "sharpest on task 1", because the level this task settles on bills
`at_trip_start` and the write lands the day before the trip starts. The base sentence is now named
in `overwrite` and replaced by "The protection fee for a trip is charged once against the election
that carries the cover, on the level the election stands on and for the days of cover the election
carries" (`guestplan.extended.yaml:1576-1581`). **The residual now/wait ambiguity revision 1
disclaimed is gone**: the charter no longer carries a sentence saying the fee falls due at the
level's billing point, so no reading of it defers this write to 2026-06-02. Acting now is the only
reading. This is a strict improvement on this task's unique-solution argument. It leaves R2-O1
(an orphaned base parameter), recorded charter-globally and with no consequence here.

**Edit C — the base charged-days sentence is now declared superseded in this policy too (round-1
F-7).** `guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment.overwrite` now names "Charged days are the whole
days of the trip as reserved…" and replaces it with "The charged days are the election's covered
days, never fewer than the level's minimum charge days." Revision 1 held that the merged semantics
were already unique because the sibling policy `guestplan_ext_level_election_cover` retired the
same base sentence; the second declaration makes the supersession local to the policy that relies
on it. Both replacements are jointly determinate (`charged_days = MX(covered_days,
level_min_charge_days)` = MX(81, 1) = 81), so **no second value for `days_covered` arises, and the

### policy_self_consistency_r3 (this task only)

#### This task's revision-2 pass rested on a tie that agreed by luck

At revisions 1 and 2 this task's scored fee was 3272.03, reached through

`3806.25 × 0.95 = 3615.9375`, `× 0.88 = 3182.025`, `+ 90.00 = 3272.025` → `RND(3272.025)`.

**3272.025 is an exact half-cent.** The nearest double to it is
**3272.025000000000090949…**, i.e. **above**, so the evaluator returned 3272.03 — which is also what
half-up gives. The two agreed. But they agreed *because of where the binary representation fell*,
not because the policy said anything that fixes a tie: at revision 2 no rounding mode was stated
anywhere — not in the rule, not in `baseline.rule`, not in the tool contract. Had the double fallen
below, as it does for 296.405 at the identically-shaped rounding point in task 0, the evaluator
would have scored **3272.02** while every stated reading gives 3272.03, and this task would have
failed on exactly the ground task 0 did.

The same tie sat on this task's `mileage_exposure_step` **sensitivity**, `RND(3182.025)`, agreeing
for the same reason.

**This audit saw the coincidence and did not name it.** Revision 1 §`findings` T1-O2 recorded that
"a reader who rounds early … still lands on 3,272.03" and called it "a property of this world's
figures rather than a defect". That observation was standing on the tie — an early-rounding reader
lands on the same figure precisely because the quantity is a half-cent that both paths resolve the
same way. The right question was not whether two reading orders agree, but whether the exact
arithmetic lands on a half-cent at all, and that question was not asked until this round. **A pass
that rests on a representation coincidence is not an entailment**, and this task's revisions 1 and 2
are corrected in that respect here, without their text being altered.

#### How the fix lands on this task

`returning_fee_rate` moves 0.95 → 0.94. This task's guest sits on that tier — three base-rate trips
inside twelve months, no mileage overage inside it — so the tier taken is unchanged and only its
value moves. The fee becomes `3806.25 × 0.94 = 3577.875`, `× 0.88 = 3148.53` **exactly**, and
`+ 90.00 = 3238.53` with **no rounding required at all**. The tie is gone by construction, not by
resolution.

- **The rounding mode** is now stated in this policy's `rule`, its `baseline.rule` and its tool
  contract. **R3-F1 does not touch this policy** — the one policy that kept an unmoded rounding
  sentence is `guestplan_ext_level_change_difference`, which is task 0's.

(the only one at `MONTHS = 13`), which is the returning tier on both generations. Only the tier's
value moved, 0.95 → 0.94. Then `3806.25 × 0.94 = 3577.875`, `× 0.88 = 3148.53` **exactly**, above
the 38.00 floor and under the 3200.00 ceiling, `+ 90.00 = 3238.53` — **a figure that requires no
rounding at all.** The tie is removed by construction rather than resolved by a convention, which is
the stronger of the two available fixes.

`covered_days_count` correctly did not move: `guestplan_ext_level_election_cover` computes over
integers with no `RND`, so it never had a tie and nothing in this round touches it.

## findings_r3

### The tie under this task — CLOSED, and this audit's earlier passes corrected

Verified with an independent exact-rational implementation:

- the quantity that was `RND(3272.025)` — an exact half-cent agreeing with half up only because the
  nearest double lies above it — is now **3238.53 reached exactly**, with no rounding point at all;
- the `mileage_exposure_step` sensitivity that was `RND(3182.025)` is now **3148.53**, likewise
  exact;
- across this task's 9 figures, **0 of 9** reach a rounding point on an exact half-cent, against
  **2 of 9** at revision 2;
- the ladder keeps three distinct outcomes (0.90 / **0.94** / 1.00) with its ordering and its
  tier-taken unchanged.

**What this costs this audit's own record.** Revision 1 and revision 2 both passed this task's
unique-solution relationship on a figure that no published sentence entailed. Revision 1 §`findings`
**T1-O2** came within one sentence of the defect — it noted that an early-rounding reader "still
lands on 3,272.03" and judged the coincidence harmless — and revision 2 re-tested T1-O2 and
confirmed it unchanged. Both were looking at the tie and asking the wrong question of it. The right
question is not whether two reading orders agree on the output, but **whether the exact arithmetic
lands on a half-cent at all**; an agreeing tie is invisible to every output comparison, because both
sides print the same number. That question is now part of this audit and is answered for all 33
figures of the difficulty in `_difficulty.md` §`the_tie_sweep`.

T1-O2 is therefore **superseded**: its factual content (the ceiling is selected and not reached, and
the factor still bears weight) survives and is re-verified — 1290.00 against 3238.53 — but its
closing remark about early rounding was an unrecognised report of the defect, and should not be read
as a clean bill.
